newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Scot Hydro raises profits, sales up.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Scot Hydro raises profits, sales up.

text.p: British electricity generator Scottish Hydro-Electric Plc turned in higher year profits as expected on Thursday, hiked its dividend 12 percent and said sales had increased further in the current year.
"The new financial year has started well, with a further increase in sales volume," chairman Lord Wilson of Tillyorn said in a statement.
Pretax profits for the year ending March 31 rose to 205.4 million pounds ($335.4 million) from 195.1 million previously with a total dividend of 17.64 pence.
The results along with bid talk in the sector boosted all British utilities' shares on Thursday. Scottish Hydro shares were up 7.5 pence by 0920 GMT to 428.5 pence, off a high of 430 pence.
"We think they are one of the best in the sector...and the outlook for them is bright," said one trader.
The company said current investment plans should take gearing to around 65 percent by 1999 from current levels of 52.1 percent with interest cover falling to around six times.
"With a strong balance sheet we will continue to seek out new investment opportunities," Lord Wilson said.
Chief executive Roger Young told Reuters that the company would be "happy to see interest cover drop towards...four times and that would be gearing in the 80-90 percent range," to fund investments.
He said projects under consideration were all in electricity generation, including combined heat and power (CHP) plants.
"We have got a number of projects around which could use that balance sheet firepower," he said.

The company bought out its 50 percent joint venture partner, United Utilities, from the Keadby power station in February for 122.7 million pounds and also has a venture with BG Plc for a gas-fired power station near Bristol, western England.

Plants currently under construction are expected to bring the company's market share of generation in Britain to eight percent in 1999 but Young said that level was "a step on the road to further increases, providing always that the economics stack up."
Scottish Hydro has around 30 percent of Scotland's generation market and just three percent in England and Wales currently.
The company said it aimed to produce "significant real dividend growth," adding that it was prepared to reduce "modestly" its present level of dividend cover over the next few years to achieve this.
Young said the company could see dividend cover ease to two times from current levels of 2.38 times.
"I think we've indicated that we would go down towards two...we wouldn't want to go below that in the foreseeable future," he said.
He added that the key thing was to ensure that the dividend grew "in a stable way."
The company, which specialises in hydro-electric generation, said dry weather last year cost it around six million pounds.
"Because it was quite dry, our hydro output was lower than normal," although better than the previous, extremely dry, year, Young said.
"We had to burn coal rather than use rainfall to the extent of about six million pounds," he added.

Scottish Hydro is aiming to compete in the British electricity supply market in 1998 when it is opened up to competition and is "pursuing a number of possible ways into the English market," Young said.
It hopes to maintain market share in Scotland as losses in its monopoly in the north of the country are offset by gains in the south.
But Young pointed out that the company was "not pursuing market share, we are pursuing profit."
But he denied the company had made excess profits as defined under the new Labour government's proposals for a one-off tax on privatised utilities.
Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown has said the tax would be on the excess profits of privatised utilities and aims to make it a central plank of a first budget on July 2.

"We've been picking up on the Chancellor's statement that he was planning to tax excess profits...the shareholders of Hydro-Electric have not actually had excess returns," Young said. ($ = 0.612 British Pounds)
